The answer is probably all of the above, and what a kinetic, eccentric, furiously exciting show James Graham and his director Daniel Evans have crafted.
It's not perfect now — there are still too many distracting bells and whistles; tantalising ideas are left hanging — but it's sharper and more streamlined.
Due largely to his forensically investigative approach and balanced presentation of the subject matter, James Graham’s latest play Quiz has managed to deliver both on style and substance.

cn.t: Graham's clever play about the "Coughing Major" scandal delivers a sparkling, forensically balanced examination of truth and doubt that's both witty and wise, confirming him as a top-tier political playwright.
